# AgIsoStack.VirtualTerminal

> An ISOBUS virtual terminal (ISO 11783-6) for .NET 10 on macOS, Linux, Windows, iOS and Android:
> AgIsoStack++'s VT server run on one thread (one to four terminals, as displays in one cab), with
> each terminal's shown screen sent out as a JSON draw list for a page to paint. The host supplies CAN frames, a page, and optionally pool storage. MIT.

Implements bring their own UI (object pools), so a host designs no screens. It forwards JSON to a
page and turns touches into calls. Package `AgIsoStack.VirtualTerminal`, namespace `AgIsoStack`.

Rules an integration must keep:

- One `VirtualTerminalStack` per process, with `Count` (1 to 4) terminals in `stack.Terminals`; each
  `VirtualTerminal` has its own events and calls. Implements choose their terminal (in their own
  menu); the host can't move them. Call `stack.Start()` before the link, and stop the link before
  `stack.Stop()`.
- Every event and every `IPoolStore` call comes on the stack's own thread. Marshal to the UI with
  a non-blocking post (BeginInvoke, Post); never a synchronous Invoke or `.Wait()` from a handler.
  Keep handlers short: the bus waits on them.
- Calls (`SoftKeyAsync`, `ButtonAsync`, `SelectAsync`, `SetNumberAsync`, `SetStringAsync`,
  `EscapeAsync`, `ActivateAsync`) work from any thread and return tasks. They fail with
  `InvalidOperationException` when the stack isn't running.
- `Send` (in options) runs on the stack's thread and its span is valid only during the call:
  copy it, queue it, return. `Receive` and `AowLink.Send` work from any thread.
- Every key or button press must end in `Released` or `Aborted`. Send only the press and its end:
  the stack repeats `Held` every 200 ms while a key is down.
- Input numbers are raw: shown = (raw + offset) * scale. `SetNumberAsync` takes raw, within min..max.
- Drive the field editor from `edit` messages (`"o": null` closes it), not from your own calls.
- Keep pictures from the `Image` event for the life of the terminal; screens refer to them by id.
- Don't give it a store that refuses to save: implements told "not stored" disconnect. The
  default store keeps pools in memory; `FilePoolStore` keeps them on disk.
- The bus: `AowLink` (a gateway over TCP) or `SlcanLink` (an slcan adapter on this device's serial
  port or, on Android, USB; not iOS), both wired with `stack.Attach(link)` and `Send = link.Send`.
  `AowLinkBrowser` finds gateways on the network (DNS-SD `_aowlink._tcp`) for the operator to pick
  by name.
- Subscribe to `HandlerFailed`: exceptions in handlers and stores go there, not to the caller.

Minimal host:

```csharp
var link = new AowLink(gatewayHost, name: "My terminal");
var stack = new VirtualTerminalStack(new VirtualTerminalOptions { Send = link.Send, Store = new FilePoolStore(poolDir) });
stack.Attach(link);
stack.HandlerFailed += e => log(e);
var vt = stack.Terminals[0];
vt.Message += json => page.Post(json);   // screen, edit, workingSets, alarms, audio, volume, identify
vt.Image += image => page.PostImage(image);
stack.Start();
link.Start();
```
